sn47.22:1.2: Sitting to one side the Venerable Bhadda said to the Venerable Ānanda:
sn47.22:1.3: “Friend Ānanda, what is the cause and reason why the true Dhamma does not endure long after a Tathagata has attained final Nibbāna?
sn47.22:1.4: And what is the cause and reason why the true Dhamma endures long after a Tathagata has attained final Nibbāna?”
sn47.22:2.2: Your intelligence is excellent, your acumen is excellent, your inquiry is a good one.
sn47.22:2.4: ‘Friend Ānanda, what is the cause and reason why the true Dhamma does not endure long after a Tathagata has attained final Nibbāna?
sn47.22:2.5: And what is the cause and reason why the true Dhamma endures long after a Tathagata has attained final Nibbāna?’”
sn47.22:2.7: “It is, friend, because the four establishments of mindfulness are not developed and cultivated that the true Dhamma does not endure long after a Tathagata has attained final Nibbāna.
sn47.22:2.8: And it is because the four establishments of mindfulness are developed and cultivated that the true Dhamma endures long after a Tathagata has attained final Nibbāna.
sn47.22:3.2: Here, friend, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body …
sn47.22:3.5: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.22:3.6: “It is because these four establishments of mindfulness are not developed and cultivated that the true Dhamma does not endure long after a Tathagata has attained final Nibbāna.
sn47.22:3.7: And it is because these four establishments of mindfulness are developed and cultivated that the true Dhamma endures long after a Tathagata has attained final Nibbāna.”
